# Adjudication Task — Chapter 162

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃162화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그런 순간이 있다. 시끌벅적하고 빈틈없이 맞물린 소음이 갑자기 사라지는 순간이. 지금이 바로 그랬다.
  6|
  7|끼이이이익.
  8|
  9|낡은 문이 열리는 소리에 소란스럽던 객잔 안이 조용해졌다.
 10|
 11|산서성을 발칵 뒤집어 놓을 계획을 세우고 축배를 들던 네 명의 우두머리와 이백여 명에 이르는 마적, 유목민들의 시선이 모두 입구를 향해 쏠렸다.
 12|
 13|저벅. 저벅. 저벅.
 14|
 15|‘저건…….’
 16|
 17|천천히 자신들을 향해 걸어오는 불청객을 확인한 흑사(黑蛇)의 눈이 가늘어졌다.
 18|
 19|‘웬 노인네야?’
 20|
 21|불청객의 정체는 노인(老人). 말 그대로 늙은 사람이다.
 22|
 23|그러나 흑사는 지금 다가오는 저 노인보다 늙은 사람을 본 적이 없었다.
 24|
 25|‘거의 시체 수준이군.’
 26|
 27|금방이라도 쓰러질 듯 비틀거리는 걸음걸이, 쭈글쭈글한 피부는 꽁꽁 얼어 있었고 내뱉는 숨은 가늘기만 했다.
 28|
 29|가만히 노인을 지켜보던 테무르와 칭겐, 인도가 대화를 주고받았다.
 30|
 31|“저 정도로 늙은 사람은 처음 보는군. 우리 부족의 주술사보다 더 늙었어.”
 32|
 33|“그런데 웬 늙은이지? 행색은 또 왜 저렇고?”
 34|
 35|“마적이라도 만났나 보지.”
 36|
 37|말마따나 노인의 행색은 초라하기 그지없었다. 어디서 낭패라도 당했는지 걸치고 있는 옷은 너덜너덜했고, 살가죽만 남은 몸뚱어리가 훤히 보였다.
 38|
 39|“재수도 없는 늙은이군. 기껏 살아남아 온 곳이 마적 소굴이니.”
 40|
 41|인도가 혀를 찼다.
 42|
 43|“저런 늙은이는 죽이고 싶은 마음도 안 든다. 치워라.”
 44|
 45|“옛.”
 46|
 47|인도의 수하가 나서려던 그때였다.
 48|
 49|“잠깐.”
 50|
 51|손을 들어 제지한 사람은 흑사였다. 노인을 응시하는 그의 미간이 좁아졌다.
 52|
 53|‘뭔가 이상하다.’
 54|
 55|그들이 머물고 있는 이 객잔은 마적들에 의해 만들어졌다. 때문에 주인, 숙수, 점소이도 모두 마적이거나 마적 출신이다.
 56|
 57|북부 고원 유일의 중립지이기 때문에 오늘 같은 화합이나 화해의 장이 되기도 했다.
 58|
 59|‘그런데 이런 곳에 제 발로 기어와? 그것도 저런 늙은이가?’
 60|
 61|북부 고원에 발을 디딘 자라면 객잔의 존재 또한 당연히 안다.
 62|
 63|평범한 양민이 출입했다가는 죽은 목숨이라는 사실도.
 64|
 65|“왜 그러시오?”
 66|
 67|“쉿, 잠시 기다리게. 어째 심상치 않아.”
 68|
 69|흑사의 반응에 다른 이들도 문득 이상함을 느끼기 시작했다.
 70|
 71|“그러고 보니 여긴 어떻게 왔지?”
 72|
 73|“외지인 같은데…….”
 74|
 75|“외지인은 아니다. 저런 늙은이가 몸 성히 여기까지 왔을 리 없어.”
 76|
 77|북부 고원에는 수백 개의 마적단과 유목 부족이 흩어져 있다. 어지간히 간덩이가 붓지 않고서야 혈혈단신의 몸으로 고원을 가로지를 생각은 하지 못한다.
 78|
 79|흑사를 포함한 네 사람은 각자 생각에 잠겼다.
 80|
 81|‘혹시……?’
 82|
 83|‘무림인이라면 가능하지.’
 84|
 85|‘무림인? 저 노인네가?’
 86|
 87|‘신경 쓰인다. 죽여야겠어.’
 88|
 89|특히나 인도에게 살인이란 숨 쉬는 것과 별반 다를 바가 없다. 거침없이 검갑에 손을 가져가는 그를 흑사가 노려봤다.
 90|
 91|이어 인도의 귓가를 파고드는 한 줄기 전음.
 92|
 93|- 기다리라고 했네. 좀 더 지켜본 후에 움직여도 늦지 않아. 무림에서는 여자와 아이, 노인을 조심하라는 말도 못 들어 봤나?
 94|
 95|- 걱정도 유분수군. 저런 비루먹은 늙은이가?
 96|
 97|- 경거망동하지 말게. 무림에서는 어떤 일이 벌어질지 몰라.
 98|
 99|툭 치면 죽을 것 같은 늙은이다. 그러나 흑사의 경고를 무시할 수도 없었다.
100|
101|인도가 짜증 섞인 한숨과 함께 검갑을 내려놨다.
102|
103|- 잘 생각했네.
104|
105|그사이 정체불명의 노인은 후들거리는 발걸음으로 네 사람의 앞까지 도달해 있었다.
106|
107|묘한 긴장감이 흐르는 가운데, 흐릿한 눈빛으로 주위를 둘러본 노인이 입을 열었다.
108|
109|“무, 물 좀…….”
110|
111|물을 찾는 바짝 마른 목소리에 사람들이 그럼 그렇지, 하는 얼굴로 고개를 저었다.
112|
113|하지만 흑사만큼은 달랐다. 치밀하고 용의주도한 성격인 그는 마지막까지 경계를 풀지 않았다.
114|
115|“노인장께서 목이 타시는 모양이다. 시원한 물을 가져다드려라.”
116|
117|“존명.”
118|
119|마적에게서 잔을 건네받은 노인이 허겁지겁 물을 들이켰다. 어찌나 급하게 마시는지 저러다가 쓰러지지는 않을까 걱정이 될 정도였다.
120|
121|노인은 연거푸 대여섯 잔을 들이켜고 나서야 고개를 들었다.
122|
123|“후우.”
124|
125|“이제 좀 괜찮으시오?”
126|
127|노인의 쭈글쭈글한 얼굴 위로 함박웃음이 번졌다.
128|
129|“네!”
130|
131|“……?”
132|
133|“감사합니다, 아저씨!”
134|
135|아저씨라니? 당황한 흑사가 벌떡 일어나 노인의 손목을 잡아챘다.
136|
137|아무런 저항도, 힘도 없다. 앙상한 뼈는 조금이라도 힘을 주면 부러질 것 같았다.
138|
139|“이보시오, 노인장?”
140|
141|“네? 왜요?”
142|
143|어린아이 같은 웃음과 말투. 노인을 물끄러미 바라보던 흑사의 얼굴이 일그러졌다.
144|
145|“젠장. 정신 나간 노인네로군.”
146|
147|맥이 탁 풀렸다. 분명히 뭔가 이상한 느낌을 받았는데…… 전부 기분 탓이었던 모양이다.
148|
149|아무래도 큰일을 앞두고 있다 보니 신경이 곤두설 수밖에 없었다.
150|
151|고개를 절레절레 흔드는 흑사를 인도가 비웃었다.
152|
153|“무림에서는 어떤 일이 벌어질지 모른다더니. 그 말이 꼭 맞았군. 노환(老患)에 시달리는 노인이라니. 크하하!”
154|
155|“그 주둥이 닥치게.”
156|
157|퉁명스럽게 대꾸한 흑사가 노인의 손목을 놓으려던 그때였다.
158|
159|“여긴 또 어디여?”
160|
161|아까와는 전혀 다른 카랑카랑한 목소리. 어느새 또렷해진 눈빛으로 사방을 둘러본 노인이 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
162|
163|“염병할. 늙으면 죽어야지.”
164|
165|척 보아하니 이제야 제정신으로 돌아온 모양. 노인의 푸념에 곳곳에서 웃음이 새어 나왔다.
166|
167|완전히 여유를 되찾은 흑사도 피식 웃으며 물었다.
168|
169|“노인장, 이제 정신이 드시오?”
170|
171|노인이 대답했다.
172|
173|“어린노무 새끼가 어디서 하오체야? 하오문 출신이냐?”
174|
175|“……어?”
176|
177|“손목은 또 왜 잡고 있어? 나랑 정분나고 싶어?”
178|
179|“이, 이보시오.”
180|
181|“놔, 안 놔? 셋 센다. 하나, 둘, 셋.”
182|
183|휙. 엉겁결에 손목을 놔 버린 흑사는 갑작스러운 상황에 정신이 하나도 없었다.
184|
185|‘이 늙은이, 도대체 뭐지?’
186|
187|걸쭉한 욕설, 다다다 쏘아붙이는 말에 저절로 몸이 움직였다.
188|
189|분명 무공 한 줄 모르는 정신 나간 노인에 불과한데…… 귀신에라도 홀린 기분이었다.
190|
191|“크하하하! 아주 제대로 당했군!”
192|
193|인도가 광소를 터트렸다. 안 그래도 무공으로 치자면 한 수 아래인 흑사가 대장 노릇을 하던 것이 마음에 안 들던 차였다.
194|
195|그런 상황에서 흑사가 정신이 오락가락하는 늙은이에게 망신당하는 걸 보니 속이 다 후련했다.
196|
197|“늙은이가 입담이 아주 제법이군. 덕분에 크게 웃었으니 살려 줘야겠어.”
198|
199|하지만 인도의 입가에 걸린 흡족한 미소가 사라지기까지는 그리 오랜 시간이 필요하지 않았다.
200|
201|노인의 입에서 튀어나온 한마디 때문이었다.
202|
203|“이런 호래자식이…… 넌 애미 애비도 없냐?”
204|
205|“……!”
206|
207|순간 객잔 안이 싸늘한 침묵에 잠겼다.
208|
209|흑사와 인도가 누구인가. 북부 고원을 주름잡는 거물들이다. 세력도 세력이지만 스스로도 어지간한 마적단 하나를 우습게 박살 내는 절정 고수들.
210|
211|존경과 두려움을 한 몸에 받는 두 사람을 노인은 말 몇 마디로 난도질해 버렸다.
212|
213|“한 놈은 하오문 출신 남색가고, 한 놈은 부모도 없이 자라서 혓바닥이 반 토막 난 놈. 그리고 나머지 두 놈은……”
214|
215|변발을 한 테무르와 칭겐을 슬쩍 바라본 노인이 한숨을 내쉬었다.
216|
217|“젊은 놈들이 벌써부터 이마가 다 까졌군. 불쌍한지고.”
218|
219|이제는 더 이상 놀랄 기력도 없다. 충격과 공포에 휩싸인 분위기 속, 쯧쯧 혀를 찬 노인이 네 사람 앞에 놓인 음식을 발견하고 눈을 크게 떴다.
220|
221|“아따, 한 상 우라지게 차려 놨네. 배고팠는데 잘됐다.”
222|
223|누가 말릴 새도 없었다.
224|
225|잘 구워진 오리 한 마리를 집어 든 노인이 다리를 잡고 북 뜯었다.
226|
227|“햐, 살코기 야들야들한 것 보소. 아주 혀에서 살살 녹는다, 녹아.”
228|
229|우걱우걱.
230|
231|다리 두 쪽을 게 눈 감추듯 해치운 노인이 분노와 충격으로 몸을 부르르 떨고 있는 인도에게 대뜸 살점을 쓱 내밀었다.
232|
233|“아직 젊은 놈이 왜 이렇게 몸을 떨어 대? 몸이 허해서 골골거리지 말고 이거나 먹어. 나는 퍽퍽한 가슴살은 싫, 아니 못 먹어. 이가 안 좋아서.”
234|
235|뚜둑.
236|
237|객잔에 있던 모든 사람이 같은 소리를 들었다.
238|
239|그건 인도의 마지막 이성의 끈이 끊어지는 소리였고, 한 사람의 죽음을 예고하는 단말마였다.
240|
241|“이 개 같은 늙은이가!”
242|
243|다음 순간, 눈이 뒤집힌 인도의 신형이 번개처럼 솟구쳤다. 동시에 그의 손에 들린 참마검(斬馬劍)에서 줄기줄기 쏟아진 핏빛 검기가 전방을 휩쓸었다.
244|
245|“이런 미친!”
246|
247|“피해!”
248|
249|콰과광!
250|
251|테무르와 칭겐이 몸을 빼기 무섭게 굉음이 터져 나왔다.
252|
253|수백, 수천 개의 나무 조각이 사방으로 튀었고 먼지 구름이 휘몰아쳤다.
254|
255|“죽어! 죽어! 죽어!”
256|
257|그 광경을 지켜보던 이들은 모골이 송연해졌다. 지금 인도에게서 느껴지는 광기를 보건대, 노인은 육편(肉片) 하나 남기지 못하고 죽었을 게 뻔했다.
258|
259|“정신 나간 늙은이가 감히! 크아아악!”
260|
261|콰과과광!
262|
263|쉼 없이 쏟아지는 검기의 향연. 마침내 인도가 참마검을 거둬들인 것은 일다경이 지난 후였다.
264|
265|“후우, 후우…….”
266|
267|거친 숨을 몰아쉬던 인도가 허공에 검을 휘둘렀다. 그러자 검압에 의해 먼지구름이 흩어지며 반쯤 가루가 된 폐허가 모습을 드러냈다.
268|
269|모두의 짐작처럼 노인은 그 어디에도 보이지 않았다.
270|
271|“내가 본 가장 용감한 사람이었어.”
272|
273|“노인장, 잘 가시오.”
274|
275|“그러니까 어쩌자고 인도를 건드려서…….”
276|
277|“역시 한족 놈들, 엄청나게 포악하군.”
278|
279|이백여 명의 마적과 유목민들이 작은 목소리로 수군거리던 그때였다.
280|
281|우적우적. 꿀꺽. 크허!
282|
283|“……?”
284|
285|“……?”
286|
287|“……?”
288|
289|처음에 느낀 것은 황당함이었다. 이 분위기 속에서 어떤 눈치 없는 놈이 음식과 술을 먹는단 말인가.
290|
291|그러나 물음표가 느낌표로, 황당함이 경악으로 바뀌는 데까지는 촌각이면 충분했다.
292|
293|“느, 늙은이! 늙은이가 살아 있다!”
294|
295|“뭣이! 어디?”
296|
297|“뒤다! 뒤에서 들렸어!”
298|
299|누군가의 외침. 그리고 모두가 귀를 의심케 할 카랑카랑한 목소리가 이어졌다.
300|
301|“요즘 놈들은 참 싸가지가 없어서 문제야. 내 이름이 늙은이냐? 네 친구야?”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 162

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃162화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그런 순간이 있다. 시끌벅적하고 빈틈없이 맞물린 소음이 갑자기 사라지는 순간이. 지금이 바로 그랬다.
  6|
  7|끼이이이익.
  8|
  9|낡은 문이 열리는 소리에 소란스럽던 객잔 안이 조용해졌다.
 10|
 11|산서성을 발칵 뒤집어 놓을 계획을 세우고 축배를 들던 네 명의 우두머리와 이백여 명에 이르는 마적, 유목민들의 시선이 모두 입구를 향해 쏠렸다.
 12|
 13|저벅. 저벅. 저벅.
 14|
 15|‘저건…….’
 16|
 17|천천히 자신들을 향해 걸어오는 불청객을 확인한 흑사(黑蛇)의 눈이 가늘어졌다.
 18|
 19|‘웬 노인네야?’
 20|
 21|불청객의 정체는 노인(老人). 말 그대로 늙은 사람이다.
 22|
 23|그러나 흑사는 지금 다가오는 저 노인보다 늙은 사람을 본 적이 없었다.
 24|
 25|‘거의 시체 수준이군.’
 26|
 27|금방이라도 쓰러질 듯 비틀거리는 걸음걸이, 쭈글쭈글한 피부는 꽁꽁 얼어 있었고 내뱉는 숨은 가늘기만 했다.
 28|
 29|가만히 노인을 지켜보던 테무르와 칭겐, 인도가 대화를 주고받았다.
 30|
 31|“저 정도로 늙은 사람은 처음 보는군. 우리 부족의 주술사보다 더 늙었어.”
 32|
 33|“그런데 웬 늙은이지? 행색은 또 왜 저렇고?”
 34|
 35|“마적이라도 만났나 보지.”
 36|
 37|말마따나 노인의 행색은 초라하기 그지없었다. 어디서 낭패라도 당했는지 걸치고 있는 옷은 너덜너덜했고, 살가죽만 남은 몸뚱어리가 훤히 보였다.
 38|
 39|“재수도 없는 늙은이군. 기껏 살아남아 온 곳이 마적 소굴이니.”
 40|
 41|인도가 혀를 찼다.
 42|
 43|“저런 늙은이는 죽이고 싶은 마음도 안 든다. 치워라.”
 44|
 45|“옛.”
 46|
 47|인도의 수하가 나서려던 그때였다.
 48|
 49|“잠깐.”
 50|
 51|손을 들어 제지한 사람은 흑사였다. 노인을 응시하는 그의 미간이 좁아졌다.
 52|
 53|‘뭔가 이상하다.’
 54|
 55|그들이 머물고 있는 이 객잔은 마적들에 의해 만들어졌다. 때문에 주인, 숙수, 점소이도 모두 마적이거나 마적 출신이다.
 56|
 57|북부 고원 유일의 중립지이기 때문에 오늘 같은 화합이나 화해의 장이 되기도 했다.
 58|
 59|‘그런데 이런 곳에 제 발로 기어와? 그것도 저런 늙은이가?’
 60|
 61|북부 고원에 발을 디딘 자라면 객잔의 존재 또한 당연히 안다.
 62|
 63|평범한 양민이 출입했다가는 죽은 목숨이라는 사실도.
 64|
 65|“왜 그러시오?”
 66|
 67|“쉿, 잠시 기다리게. 어째 심상치 않아.”
 68|
 69|흑사의 반응에 다른 이들도 문득 이상함을 느끼기 시작했다.
 70|
 71|“그러고 보니 여긴 어떻게 왔지?”
 72|
 73|“외지인 같은데…….”
 74|
 75|“외지인은 아니다. 저런 늙은이가 몸 성히 여기까지 왔을 리 없어.”
 76|
 77|북부 고원에는 수백 개의 마적단과 유목 부족이 흩어져 있다. 어지간히 간덩이가 붓지 않고서야 혈혈단신의 몸으로 고원을 가로지를 생각은 하지 못한다.
 78|
 79|흑사를 포함한 네 사람은 각자 생각에 잠겼다.
 80|
 81|‘혹시……?’
 82|
 83|‘무림인이라면 가능하지.’
 84|

The man was clearly nothing more than a deranged old fool who did not know a single martial art, yet Black Sand felt as though he had been bewitched.

[P100]
“Ha-ha-ha-ha! He got you good!”

[P101]
The Human Butcher burst into raucous laughter. He had already resented Black Sand acting as their leader despite being a step below him in martial arts.

[P102]
Seeing Black Sand humiliated by a senile old man was deeply satisfying.

[P103]
“That old man has quite a mouth on him. He gave me a good laugh, so I suppose I’ll let him live.”

[P104]
But the satisfied smile on the Human Butcher’s face did not last long.

[P105]
A single sentence from the old man wiped it away.

[P106]
“You miserable bastard… Don’t you have a mother or father?”

[P107]
“…!”

[P108]
The inn plunged into icy silence.

[P109]
Black Sand and the Human Butcher were major figures who dominated Northern Gaoyuan. Their forces alone made them formidable, but they were also Peak masters capable of crushing an average mounted-bandit group single-handedly.

[P110]
They commanded respect and fear in equal measure, yet the old man had carved them apart with a few words.

[P111]
“One’s a sodomite from the Lower District Sect. One grew up without parents and has only half a tongue. And as for the other two…”

[P112]
The old man glanced at Temur and Chinggen, both of whom wore their hair in queues, then sighed.

[P113]
“You’re still young, but your foreheads are already bare. How pitiful.”

[P114]
No one had the energy left to be surprised. Amid the atmosphere of shock and horror, the old man clicked his tongue. Then he noticed the food spread out before the four men, and his eyes widened.

[P115]
“Well, damn. You’ve laid out one hell of a feast. I was hungry, too. Perfect.”

[P116]
No one had time to stop him.

[P117]
The old man grabbed a well-roasted duck by the leg and tore it off.

[P118]
“Would you look at how tender that meat is? Melts right on the tongue.”

[P119]
*Crunch, crunch.*

[P120]
After devouring both legs in the blink of an eye, he abruptly held out a chunk of meat to the Human Butcher, who was trembling with rage and shock.

[P121]
“You’re still young. Why are you shaking like that? Don’t go wasting away from weakness—eat this. I don’t like dry breast meat. No, I can’t eat it. My teeth are bad.”

[P122]
*Crack.*

[P123]
Everyone in the inn heard the same sound.

[P124]
It was the sound of the last thread of the Human Butcher’s reason snapping—and the death knell of a man.

[P125]
“You goddamn old bastard!”

[P126]
The next instant, the Human Butcher shot forward like a bolt of lightning, his eyes rolling back in fury. Crimson Sword Energy erupted from the horse-chopping sword in his hand and swept across everything before him.

[P127]
“What the hell!”

[P128]
“Move!”

[P129]
*Kaboom!*

[P130]
Temur and Chinggen had barely thrown themselves aside when a thunderous explosion shook the inn.

[P131]
Hundreds—thousands—of wooden fragments flew in every direction as a cloud of dust billowed through the air.

[P132]
“Die! Die! Die!”

[P133]
The sight sent chills down the onlookers’ spines. Judging by the madness pouring from the Human Butcher, the old man could not possibly have survived. There would not be so much as a scrap of flesh left.

[P134]
“How dare a senile old man—! Aaaaargh!”

[P135]
*Boom! Boom! Boom!*

[P136]
The relentless storm of Sword Energy continued. Nearly a quarter of an hour passed before the Human Butcher finally lowered his horse-chopping sword.

[P137]
“Huff… huff…”

[P138]
Breathing heavily, he swung his weapon through the air. The resulting pressure scattered the dust cloud, revealing ruins that had been half reduced to powder.

[P139]
Just as everyone had expected, the old man was nowhere to be seen.

[P140]
“He was the bravest man I’ve ever seen.”

[P141]
“Farewell, elder.”

[P142]
“Why did he have to provoke the Human Butcher…?”

[P143]
“Those Han Chinese really are unbelievably savage.”

[P144]
The more than two hundred mounted bandits and nomads were whispering among themselves when—

[P145]
*Crunch, crunch. Gulp. Guh-hup!*

[P146]
“…”

[P147]
“…”

[P148]
“…”

[P149]
At first, they were simply dumbfounded.

[P150]
What kind of clueless bastard would be eating and drinking at a time like this?

[P151]
But it took only an instant for confusion to turn to astonishment, and astonishment to horror.

[P152]
“T-The old man! The old man’s alive!”

[P153]
“What? Where?”

[P154]
“Behind us! It came from behind us!”

[P155]
Someone shouted.

[P156]
Then a sharp, clear voice followed, making everyone doubt their own ears.

[P157]
“Young people these days have no manners. Is my name ‘old man’? Am I your friend?”

[P158]
“W-Whoa!”

[P159]
“That does it. I’ll teach you bastards some manners today.”

[P160]
*Thud-thud-thud! Whoosh!*

[P161]
The mounted bandits and nomads filling the inn went flying one after another.

[P162]
Every one of them was hurled aside with mangled limbs and smashed faces. The sight made the leaders break out in cold sweats.

[P163]
*W-What is this?*

[P164]
*How did he get over there?*

[P165]
*I didn’t even see him move.*

[P166]
A master.

[P167]
A master capable of deceiving the eyes of Peak masters like them.

[P168]
Black Sand, Temur, and Chinggen went rigid. Only one man charged toward the old man.

[P169]
“You goddamn old bastard!”

[P170]
The Human Butcher had already lost all reason. Nothing could hold him back now.

[P171]
The old man saw him barreling forward and frowned.

[P172]
“You’re…”

[P173]
“That’s right! It’s me! This time, I’ll kill you for sure!”

[P174]
“So you’re the one without parents.”

[P175]
“Graaaargh!”

[P176]
*Whoooosh!*

[P177]
*Mount Tai Presses Down on the Crown.*

[P178]
The horse-chopping sword blazed with crimson Sword Energy as it descended to split the old man’s skull.

[P179]
At that moment, the old man swung something.

[P180]
*Slice! Thud!*

[P181]
Time seemed to stop.

[P182]
Not a single breath could be heard. Everyone stared in disbelief.

[P183]
The horse-chopping sword had been cut in half.

[P184]
And in the old man’s hand was something tiny.

[P185]
“T-That’s…”

[P186]
For the first time, sanity returned to the Human Butcher’s eyes. He stared at the old man in fear and astonishment.

[P187]
“…A chicken bone?”

[P188]
“No part of a chicken goes to waste. The meat tastes good, the bones make a fine broth when you simmer them long enough, and sometimes they’re even handy for wielding Sword Energy.”

[P189]
Sword Energy wielded through a chicken bone.

[P190]
The Human Butcher had never seen or heard of anything so bizarre.

[P191]
He understood instinctively.

[P192]
*A master. A Supreme Peak master. Someone I could never hope to fight.*

[P193]
The old man looked at the stunned Human Butcher and muttered,

[P194]
“Come to think of it… You’re a vicious one. The stench of blood is pouring off your entire body.”

[P195]
Every word sent goose bumps crawling across the Human Butcher’s skin. He had lived his entire life as a predator, yet now he was no more than a rat before a tiger.

[P196]
“Can’t leave someone like you running around…”

[P197]
A sudden chill swept through the Human Butcher. His teeth chattered at the deadly aura seeping from the old man’s entire body.

[P198]
“P-Please.”

[P199]
“Hm?”

[P200]
“Please spare me. Please…”

[P201]
Tears ran down his cheeks. His trousers grew damp, and the horse-chopping sword slipped from his limp hand.

[P202]
The Human Butcher had spent his life taking the lives of others. No one could believe they were now watching him beg for his own.

[P203]
The old man stared at him for a moment, then spoke.

[P204]
“Don’t be afraid.”

[P205]
*I’m safe. I’m alive! I escaped death!*

[P206]
The Human Butcher let out an involuntary sigh of relief.

[P207]
That was when—

[P208]
*Thump.*

[P209]
A rough, wrinkled hand, its knuckles jutting sharply beneath the skin, pressed against his chest.

[P210]
That was the end.

[P211]
“…Huh?”

[P212]
The world turned upside down with his faint murmur. Blood flowed from the seven orifices of his fallen body and soaked the floor.

[P213]
*He said he’d spare me. Why?*

[P214]
As his vision dimmed and the sounds around him receded, he heard the old man speak.

[P215]
“Don’t be afraid. I’ll send you off without pain.”

[P216]
The old man had told the truth.

[P217]
There was no pain.

[P218]
* * *

[P219]
The Human Butcher.

[P220]
A Peak master whose evil reputation had spread all the way to the Central Plains had died in a single move.

[P221]
“Well, then…”

[P222]
The old man addressed the people frozen around him.

[P223]
“Where is this place?”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
